messages:
sam_d: running into weird combo of issues trying to wire up the Python SDK to our Dedicated instance inside a customer VPC.
sam_d: using base_url="https://inference.svc.customer.internal:8443" and passing ca_bundle to Client, but async calls error with SSL verify fail while sync requests succeed. also retries look broken behind our corporate proxy (we see 407s).

sam_d: minimal repro below — async path fails during connector init:
```py
from redwood import Client

c = Client(api_key="xxx", base_url="https://inference.svc.customer.internal:8443", ca_bundle="/etc/pki/tls/certs/customer-ca.pem")
await c.chat.create(model="redwood-beta", messages=[{"role":"user","content":"ping"}])
```

Tina_sdk: thanks — we saw a similar report. current SDK v0.12.x had two gaps: (1) Async client didn't always pass ca_bundle through when reusing pooled connectors and (2) proxy auth headers weren't being forwarded correctly for some backoff/retry cases.

Tina_sdk: quick checks: which HTTP backend is being used by async path (httpx or aiohttp)? and are you setting HTTPS_PROXY/https_proxy at the process level? some environments override TLS behavior.

sam_d: httpx. we set both https_proxy and HTTPS_PROXY. if i curl the base_url with --cacert it works.

Tina_sdk: workaround for now: set SSL_CERT_FILE/REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE to your CA path (forces OpenSSL libs and requests/httpx to use it), and set httpx transport to not reuse pool (workaround) — we can show a snippet. also add proxy creds to env var in 'http://user:pass@proxy:3128' format.

Tina_sdk: example fallback for httpx async transport:
```py
import httpx
from redwood import Client

transport = httpx.AsyncHTTPTransport(retries=2, trust_env=True)
client = Client(api_key='...', base_url='https://inference.svc.customer.internal:8443', ca_bundle='/etc/pki/tls/certs/customer-ca.pem', _httpx_transport=transport)
```

Tina_sdk: long-term: we're releasing 0.13.0 which:
- fixes AsyncClient CA/verify propagation for pooled connectors
- honors proxy auth across retries/backoff
- adds type stubs for both sync and async clients (PEP 561 .pyi files)
- exposes retry/backoff configuration on top-level Client (max_attempts, backoff_factor)

mike_infra: great — any chance to get a sample for VPC base_url patterns? our infra folks frequently forget to add the /api prefix or port.

Tina_sdk: yes we'll add a dedicated 'Dedicated/Private deployment' section to the SDK docs with examples: base_url variations, proxy env vars, CA examples, and a short troubleshooting checklist (curl with --cacert, check DNS inside VPC, check envoy host/path). i'll open a docs PR and link it here.

irene_support: verified the SSL_CERT_FILE workaround with a customer earlier today. 0.13.0 candidate fixed one customer case where httpx connector reused a default ssl.create_default_context() without the custom CA.

sam_d: nice. last question: will typed client mean my IDE (pyright/pylance) will show proper async signatures? currently type hints are very loose.

Tina_sdk: yes — typed stubs will include precise overloads for sync vs async methods, context manager types, and return types for create/streaming helpers. we also plan to publish mypy/pyright config in the repo.

Tina_sdk: i'll add you to the PR review for the docs and the typing stubs. please try the 0.13.0rc when it's available and paste logs if anything still fails.

doc-bot: PR opened: docs/sdk/dedicated-proxy-ca.md (#4123)

mike_infra: thanks, will test rc this week.

sam_d: testing now with rc — async + retries working for me. closing the loop :white_check_mark:
